object_description: articulated cross-shaped volume on three levels between bar and gable forms
geometry_property: openings on three sides per classroom
design_condition: the school is placed at the junction of the routes so that its cross shape provides four distinct outdoor spaces, two facing the village with the entrances and two facing south for play

positive: The new school makes it possible to create a real village centre with the existing buildings
The articulated volume between bar and gables reduces the visual impact of the building
The mineral coating of the public space goes around the school and extends to the existing barn and hall
The cross shape provides four distinct outdoor spaces
The two northern ones face the village and offer the different entrances
The main entrance is under cover in the extension of the village square, keeping transparency to the south
The two other outdoor spaces face south for the play areas
The clearance spaces are generous with good quality of light
The proposal for an extension to the south is appreciated and does not undermine the coherence
The cut volume is consistent with the scale of the village
The structure presents good rationality, particularly for the transmission of vertical loads
Sound insulation of the mixed floors is reinforced by a cement screed, giving better thermal inertia
The entire above-ground construction can be made of wood
negative: The jury regrets the lack of thought regarding the landscape and exterior arrangements
The two-metre difference in topography at the building is not taken into account
The absence of a low stratum and a clear planting or water strategy weakens the concept
The jury doubts the proposal for access to the north
The village square and its relationship with the parking spaces lack resolution
A ground floor classroom is positioned in window over the recreation area, making its use difficult
That room is also semi-buried on two faces because of the topography
The proportion of openings is considered too high for computerised teaching and overheating risk
The numerous storage spaces cannot only take place at the back of the room as proposed
The language of facade openings and the resulting transparency is difficult to convince
It sits awkwardly with the relatively rural and massive nature of the roof
Horizontal loads must be taken up by stabilising elements or frames in the glass facades
